title: Client renewal metric workbench - latency, uptime, cost, cache (lab)
body:
Purpose:
This is a working 'metric workbench' for Customer Success QBRs focused on renewal signals driven by operational KPIs. Goal: give CSMs a compact, consistent set of definitions, measurement sources, and action steps for the four signals we care about most for renewal conversations — latency, uptime, cost/token, cache hit rate — plus an example KPI table and a simple renewal-risk scoring recipe.

TL;DR:
- Keep definitions concrete (P95 for tail latency, rolling 7d uptime, net cost/token after discounts, cache hit by token).
- Use the same data sources and windows across customers (prometheus for latency/uptime, billing for cost, cache logs for cache hit).
- Map metric tiers to risk buckets (green/amber/red) and tie to playbooks (investigate, optimize, escalate).

Quick definitions (canonical):
- Latency (response latency): P50, P95, P99 of server-side generation time (ms). Calculation window: rolling 7d by default, show 30d trend. Exclude synthetic/healthcheck calls and warmup retries. Source: prometheus histogram (http_request_duration_seconds buckets) or inference logs aggregated by request_id.
  - Formula note: P95 = 95th percentile of end_time - start_time across successful generation requests over window.

- Uptime (availability): percentage of successful requests over total requests (or percentage of minutes with at least one healthy replica responding depending on flavor). Canonical: rolling 30d uptime measured as (successful_requests)/(total_requests) where success = 2xx or completed generation. SLAs often use 99.95% for dedicated customers; for QBR use 99.9% baseline. Source: prometheus alertmanager metrics + provider infra incident logs.
  - Edge case: if traffic is extremely low (avg < 1 req/min), fallback to 'minutes-of-availability' SLI to avoid noise.

- Cost per token (unit economics): net cost per generated token to Redwood (USD/token) averaged over window. Include GPU runtime, intermediate infra (networking, caching), and amortized model licensing costs if applicable. Exclude customer-level discounts/credits when showing Redwood OPEX; include them in 'customer billed cost' column. Window: monthly rolling and 7d spot-check. Source: billing DB + per-cluster usage tables.
  - Example calculation: cost/token = (gpu_seconds * gpu_price + storage_bytes * storage_price + egress_bytes * egress_price) / total_generated_tokens.

- Cache hit rate (token-hit fraction): fraction of generated tokens served from cache (prefix or KV) vs total generated tokens. Use token-weighted metric not request-count-weighted. Window: rolling 7d. Source: cache-proxy logs (cache_hit_tokens, total_generated_tokens).
  - Formula: cache_hit_rate = sum(cache_hit_tokens) / sum(total_generated_tokens).

Measurement windows and granularity (recommended defaults):
- Short-term operational view: 7d rolling, 1h granularity
- Strategic slant for QBR: 30d rolling, daily granularity (trend + month-over-month delta)
- Billing/econ view: 30d & 90d rolling, show monthly cohort cost/token and net revenue impact.

Canonical KPI table (example rows — paste into CS spreadsheet):
Columns: metric | window | value | baseline | trend (30d delta) | data_source | owner | action_if_degraded
Row examples (customer: AcmeAI):
- Latency P95 | 7d | 340 ms | baseline 250 ms | +40% | prometheus/gw-logs | eng-sre | run tail-stack, enable fallback variant
- Uptime | 30d | 99.87% | baseline 99.95% | -0.08% | prometheus/uptime | eng-sre | investigate recent deploys, activate reserve capacity
- Cost/token (net) | 30d | $0.0018 | baseline $0.0013 | +38% | billing-db/cluster-costs | finance-ops | check model variant, quantization plan, batching config
- Cache hit rate | 7d | 21% | baseline 45% | -24pp | cache-proxy/logs | eng-platform | surface to product for prompt-pattern review, enable prefix caching where safe

Risk mapping (simple, reproducible):
- Green: all metrics within 10% of baseline and no recent incidents in 30d
- Amber: one metric 10-50% worse than baseline OR small degradation + ongoing mitigations
- Red: any metric >50% from baseline OR uptime breach > SLA threshold OR recurring incidents without mitigation

Automated renewal signal score (example):
- Start with 100 points. Subtract points for deviations (weights): latency deviation 0.4 * %delta, uptime deviation 1.0 * hours_below_SLA_fraction*100, cost deviation 0.3 * %delta, cache degradation 0.2 * %pp_loss. Normalize to 0-100. Example: P95 +40% -> -16 pts, cost +38% -> -11.4 pts, cache -24pp -> -4.8 pts -> final ~67.8 = amber.

Playbooks (what CS should do at each tier):
- Amber actions (CS + SE): schedule a 30-min sync w/ customer, collect recent traces and example requests, propose immediate mitigations (shorter response setting, enforce burst limits, switch to lower-cap variant for heavy flows), open internal ticket with eng-platform.
- Red actions (CS + SE + ESCALATE to SRE/AE): urgent bridge, enable failover route to dedicated pool or warm standby model, discuss contractual credits if SLA broken, propose longer-term tech changes (quantization, caching strategy, batching).

Data sources & dashboards (practical):
- Latency & uptime: prometheus metrics + logs -> dashboards: CS latency quickview (P50/P95/P99 + error rates) and SRE traces (jaeger) for recent failed requests
- Cost/token: billing-db exports to bigquery -> CS econ dashboard with per-model/per-route cost allocation; reference raw cost breakdown in Finance runbook
- Cache hit: cache-proxy logs aggregated by job -> hourly token-level hits table in bigquery; augment with sample request IDs for debugging

Ownership & cadence:
- CS lead collects KPI table weekly (auto-sync spreadsheet from dashboards); SE/Platform respond to Amber within 3 business days; Red requires bridge within 24 hours.
- Owners: CS owner (customer-facing) + eng-platform (technical remediation) + finance-ops (cost clarifications).

Notes, heuristics and gotchas (collection of working knowledge):
- P95 vs P99 debate: for chat-heavy customers we prefer P95 as primary QBR metric (less noisy), but always include P99 appendices for tail events.
- Low-traffic customers: percent-based SLIs are noisy — use moving-window minimum-minute-availability or synthetic probes.
- Cost anomalies often due to model variant change or accidental high-temp sampling; always look for correlated config changes (new prompt types, too-large max_tokens param).
- Cache hit by token is more meaningful than by request for long-generation flows.

Open questions / TODOs (work items):
- [ ] Standardize cost/token attribution rules across Dedicated vs Hosted (who absorbs what). Owner: finance-ops.
- [ ] Build a 'one-click' CS export: KPI table CSV + example traces for customer-facing QBR slide. Owner: eng-platform, ticket JIRA-4028.
- [ ] Add an 'anomaly flag' column in KPI table that links to the root-cause-ticket (PRD draft in confluence). Owner: product-hosted-api.

Appendix: sample CSV export (copy-paste friendly):
metric,window,value,baseline,trend,source,owner,action
latency_p95_ms,7d,340,250,+40%,prometheus/gw-logs,eng-sre,investigate-tail
uptime_pct,30d,99.87,99.95,-0.08%,prometheus/uptime,eng-sre,check-deploys
cost_per_token_usd,30d,0.0018,0.0013,+38%,billing-db,finance-ops,review-variant
cache_hit_rate_token_pct,7d,21,45,-24pp,cache-proxy/logs,eng-platform,enable-prefix-cache

Notes-to-self: this is intentionally pragmatic than academic. When we present to customer, surface the one-liner (status + 1 action) then include the KPI table as backup. Keep the spreadsheet automation simple — we want reproducibility in 5 clicks.

History: started from CS backlog item (JIRA-3311) and internal SRE input session (2024-08). Draft owner: Aisha Patel.

If you're editing: keep short bullets, mark unresolved Qs with [ ] and tag owners.
